newsitem.title: USA: Baxter sees $6.2 bln total sales in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Baxter sees $6.2 bln total sales in 1996.

text.p: Baxter International Inc chief financial officer Harry Kraemer said the company projects sales for 1996 of about $6.2 billion, including its pending acquisition of Immuno International AG.

"For 1996 sales, we have $2 billion for IV (intravenous products); $1.3 billion for biotech, which will be $1.9 billion when you add in the Immuno International piece; $900 million for cardiovascular; and $1.4 billion for renal. That is the 1996 projected net sales," Kraemer said at a meeting on Tuesday here with reporters.
Shares in Baxter were up 1/4 to 44-7/8.
Kraemer also said the company is comfortable with the First Call consensus of 15 analysts' third-quarter earnings estimates at $0.64 per share, up from the year-ago level of $0.59 per share.
Baxter is expected to report its results for the third-quarter ending September 30 in late October.

After its spinoff of Allegiance Corp, Baxter will comprise four main business units. These units had the following sales in 1995: renal care, $1.29 billion; biotechnology, $1.13 billion; cardiovascular, $730 million; and intravenous products, $1.89 billion.

For 1997, the company projects the following sales growth rates for its four businesses, Kraemer said: renal, "12-14 percent growth;" biotechnology, "mid-teens;" cardiovascular, "low double digits;" and intravenous products, "high single digits."
"Those are the kinds of (sales) growth rates you can expect going forward," Kraemer said.

He added that Baxter expects to close its acquisition of Switzerland's Immuno by the end of the year. Afterward, he said, about 60 percent of Baxter's sales and 75 percent of profits will come from outside the United States.
